guides.why: The oil does everything in this engine: lubrication, most of the cooling, and it is shared with the clutch and gearbox. 0.7 L is not much oil for a hard-working air-cooled single, so it degrades quickly.
guides.when: 600 mi, then every 4,000 mi (6,400 km), and at least once a year. Change it sooner after lots of full-throttle, hot or dusty riding.
tools: 17 mm socket or wrench for the drain bolt (check yours)

parts.name: Gasket, drain petcock (12.5 × 20)
parts.note: New every change. #13 on the 2022 crankcase diagram

parts.name: Engine oil 10W-30, JASO MA, API SG or higher (Pro Honda GN4 or equivalent)

steps: Warm the engine for a few minutes so the oil drains fully, then put the bike on the centerstand on level ground.
Remove the drain bolt and sealing washer from the bottom of the crankcase and let it drain completely.
Fit a new sealing washer and tighten the drain bolt to 24 N·m (18 lbf·ft).
Pour in 0.7 L of oil through the filler on the right crankcase cover. Check the filler cap O-ring and replace it if it is flattened or cracked.
Start and idle 3-5 minutes, stop, wait 2-3 minutes, then check the dipstick without screwing it in. The level must be between the upper and lower marks on all faces.
checks: Capacity 0.7 L after draining, 0.9 L after engine disassembly (1-7)
pitfalls: The drain bolt threads into the aluminium case: use a torque wrench, not feel.
Read the dipstick resting on the threads, not screwed in, or it reads high.

guides.why: A fine mesh screen in the bottom of the crankcase catches debris before it reaches the oil pump. It sits behind the right crankcase cover, so do it together with the centrifugal filter.

parts.name: Gasket, R. crankcase cover
parts.note: New whenever the cover comes off

parts.name: Screen, oil filter
parts.note: Only if torn; normally cleaned and reused

parts.name: O-ring, 8 mm (clutch adjuster)
parts.note: Marked New on 2-23; #24 on the 2022 right crankcase cover diagram

steps: Drain the engine oil completely.
Remove the gearshift pedal, the step bar (footpegs) and the exhaust pipe/muffler; they block the right crankcase cover.
Loosen the right crankcase cover bolts in a crisscross pattern in several steps and remove the cover, gasket and 2 dowel pins. The kickstarter comes off with the cover.
Pull the oil strainer screen out of its slot with pliers, clean it in solvent and blow it dry.
Reinstall the screen with its tapered side facing the crankcase and the thinner edge up.
Do the centrifugal filter now while the cover is off (next guide).

Fit a new cover gasket and the dowels. When fitting the cover, align the punch mark on the clutch lever with the index line on the gearshift spindle, and seat the clutch lever on the brake plate with the spring ends on the boss.
Tighten the cover bolts crisscross. Check the kickstarter spindle oil seal; replace it if leaking.
Refill with oil, then adjust the clutch (see Clutch system).
checks: Right crankcase cover protector bolts 12 N·m (1-13)
pitfalls: Forgetting to re-adjust the clutch after refitting the cover.
Fitting the screen backwards (tapered side goes toward the crankcase).

guides.time: Adds 20 min to the strainer screen job
guides.why: This engine has no paper oil filter. A spinning drum on the crankshaft flings heavy particles outward, where they pack into a sludge layer. If it is never cleaned, the sludge can block oil flow.
guides.when: Clean at 8,000, 16,000 and 24,000 mi. Honda recommends a dealer do it (**), but it is straightforward once the right cover is off.

parts.name: Gasket, oil filter cover
parts.note: New each time; sealed side toward the cover

steps: Drain the oil and remove the right crankcase cover (strainer screen guide).
Remove the 3 bolts and the oil centrifugal filter cover from the front of the crankshaft drive plate.
Wipe the sludge out of the cover and the inside of the drive plate. Do not use anything that leaves fibres.
Fit a new gasket with its sealed side facing the filter cover.
Apply threadlocker to the 3 bolts (a 4 mm band, leaving the first 1.6 mm of the tip clean) and tighten to 5.0 N·m.
Refit the right cover, refill the oil and adjust the clutch.
checks: Filter cover bolts 5.0 N·m with locking agent (1-12)
pitfalls: 5 N·m is very light. Use an inch-pound torque wrench; the bolts strip easily.

guides.why: A worn plug causes hard starting, misfires and lost power. Inspect at 4,000-mile intervals and replace at 8,000.
guides.when: Inspect at 4,000, 12,000 and 20,000 mi; replace at 8,000, 16,000 and 24,000 mi.
tools: Spark plug wrench from the bike's tool kit (89216-KPP-900), or a 16 mm thin-wall plug socket

parts.name: Plug, spark (NGK CPR7EA-9)
parts.note: Colder plug for extended high-speed riding

steps: Remove the main pipe side cover if it blocks access to the plug cap.
Pull the plug cap straight off and clean around the plug base so dirt can't fall into the cylinder.
Remove the plug and inspect it: tan electrodes are normal; heavy carbon, oil or a white/blistered insulator point to running problems.
Set the gap to 0.8-0.9 mm.
Thread the new plug in by hand, then tighten to 16 N·m (12 lbf·ft).
checks: NGK CPR6EA-9 / Denso U20EPR9; hot riding CPR7EA-9 / U22EPR9 (1-10)
pitfalls: Cross-threading the aluminium head: always start the plug by hand.

guides.why: Valves tighten as the seats wear. Too little clearance can keep a valve from closing fully, which burns it; too much makes noise and loses power.
guides.when: Check at 4,000 mi and every 4,000 mi after (a * item: dealer job unless you have the tools). Engine must be cold, below 35 °C (95 °F).
tools: Feeler gauges 0.10 and 0.17 mm (a 0.18 mm / 0.007″ blade is within the 0.15-0.19 mm exhaust spec)
8 × 9 mm lock nut wrench (Honda 07708-0030100 or equivalent)
Valve adjusting wrench: Honda 07908-KE90200 (supersedes 07708-0030400), or a small square-drive adjuster

parts.name: O-ring, 13.8 × 2.5 (timing hole cap)
parts.note: New. #10 on the 2022 left crankcase cover diagram, under the 14 mm cap

steps: Remove the timing hole cap and crankshaft hole cap from the left crankcase cover.

Turn the crankshaft counterclockwise and align the "T" mark on the flywheel with the index notch. Check the cam sprocket mark lines up with the head notch (compression TDC); if not, turn one more full revolution.
Remove the two valve adjusting caps (2 bolts each).
Slide a feeler gauge between the adjusting screw and the valve stem. Spec: IN 0.10 ± 0.02 mm, EX 0.17 ± 0.02 mm.
To adjust, loosen the lock nut, turn the screw until there is a slight drag on the gauge, hold the screw and tighten the lock nut to 9.0 N·m (oiled). Recheck.
Refit the caps with new O-rings; timing hole cap 6.0 N·m, crankshaft hole cap 8.0 N·m. Check the idle afterwards.
pitfalls: Being on the exhaust stroke instead of compression TDC (both valves must be loose).
The clearance closes up slightly as the lock nut tightens; always recheck.

guides.why: The element is a viscous (oil-wetted) paper type. It cannot be cleaned; blowing it out with air ruins it.
guides.when: Replace at 12,000 and 24,000 mi, more often in dust or wet riding.
tools: Torque driver (1.1 N·m) or careful hands
steps: Remove the left main pipe side cover.
Remove the air cleaner cover screws and the cover.
Remove the element and check the housing for dirt or water. Wipe it out.
Fit the new element and seal, refit the cover and tighten the screws to 1.1 N·m.
pitfalls: Over-tightening the plastic cover screws strips them.

guides.why: Blow-by gas goes from the crankcase to the air box. Oil and water condense in a drain tube that has a clear section so you can see deposits.
guides.when: Every 4,000 mi, and more often after rain, full-throttle riding, washing the bike or dropping it.
steps: Find the breather drain tube at the bottom of the air cleaner housing (left side).
If you can see deposits in the clear section, remove the plug or clamp, drain it into a container and refit.
pitfalls: A full drain tube can push oil into the air filter.

guides.why: The fuel hose is a resin hose with quick-connect fittings and a fuel pump in the tank. A leak is a fire risk.
guides.when: Inspect every 4,000 mi.
steps: With the seat and fuel tank cover off, check the fuel feed hose from the pump to the injector for cracks, kinks, chafing and fuel smell.
Check that both quick-connect fittings are locked: pull on them gently.

If you disconnect anything: relieve fuel pressure first (unplug the pump connector and idle until the engine stops), never use tools on the fittings, and after reconnecting turn the key on 2-3 times to pressurize and check for leaks.
checks: Fuel pressure 263-316 kPa (38-46 psi) if you suspect a problem (2-3)
pitfalls: Bending or twisting the resin hose damages it.

forum.title: Tank / charcoal canister overfill: vent hose re-routed (hondatrail125.com)

guides.why: A sticking throttle is dangerous; too little free play can raise the idle when you turn the bars.
guides.when: Inspect every 4,000 mi.
steps: Engine off: turn the bars lock to lock and check the grip opens and snaps closed smoothly in every position.
Measure free play at the grip flange: 2-6 mm.
Adjust at the throttle cable adjuster; lock nuts 3.0-4.5 N·m.
Check the cables for kinks or fraying along their route.
pitfalls: Routing added accessory switches where they pinch the throttle cables.

guides.why: Idle is controlled by the ECM and the idle air control valve (IACV), and there is no idle screw. A wrong idle points to a fault.
guides.when: Check every 4,000 mi, with the engine warm.
steps: Warm the engine fully and check idle: 1,400 ± 100 rpm.
If idle is off, check for air leaks, a dirty throttle body and stored fault codes. After throttle body work, do the TP sensor reset.

guides.why: Fuel vapor from the tank is stored in a charcoal canister and burned by the engine. Cracked hoses mean fuel smell and, on the MIL side, code 88-1.
guides.when: Inspect at 12,000 and 24,000 mi (50-state models).
steps: Remove the right side cover.
Check the purge hoses, canister and purge control solenoid valve for cracks, loose hoses and correct routing.
checks: Purge valve resistance 37-44 Ω if code 88-1 appears (4-18)

guides.why: A dry or badly adjusted chain wears itself and the sprockets out quickly, and a very loose chain can jump off.
guides.when: Inspect and lubricate every 300 mi (500 km), and after riding in rain or dirt.
tools: Wrenches for the axle nut and adjusters

parts.name: Chain lube (Pro Honda HP Chain Lube or equivalent)

steps: Bike on the centerstand, transmission in neutral, engine off.
Measure slack on the lower run midway between the sprockets: 25-35 mm. Don't ride if it is over 50 mm.
To adjust: loosen the rear axle nut, turn both adjusters equally so the marks match on each side, then tighten the axle nut to 59 N·m.
Clean the chain with a dry cloth and high flash-point solvent, then lube it.
pitfalls: Adjusting one side more than the other misaligns the wheel.

guides.why: The slider protects the swingarm from the chain. Once it wears through, the chain cuts the swingarm.
guides.when: Inspect every 4,000 mi.
steps: Check the slider on the swingarm for grooves or wear. Replace it before the chain touches metal.

guides.why: DOT 4 absorbs water over time, which lowers its boiling point and corrodes the ABS modulator.
guides.when: Check the level at every service; replace every 2 years.
tools: 8 mm wrench for the bleed valves

parts.name: Honda DOT 4 brake fluid, from a sealed container

steps: Front: with the reservoir level, fluid must be above the LOWER mark (upper line inside the reservoir when filling). Rear (right side): between the LOWER and UPPER marks.
A falling level usually means the pads are wearing; top up only to the line.

To replace (Common Service Manual 17-9, 17-10): fit a clear hose from the bleed valve to a bottle, open the valve and pump the lever or pedal until old fluid stops, close it, and refill with fresh DOT 4. Then bleed: squeeze the lever, open the valve 1/4 turn, close it, release slowly and wait a few seconds; repeat until no bubbles come out. Top up the reservoir often so it never runs dry. Bleed valves 5.4 N·m, reservoir cap screws 1.5 N·m.
pitfalls: Brake fluid strips paint; cover the tank and plastics.
Don't let the reservoir run dry while bleeding, or air gets into the ABS modulator.

guides.time: Inspect 5 min; replace 30 min per end
guides.why: Pads worn past the indicator grooves damage the discs and lose braking.
guides.when: Inspect every 4,000 mi.
steps: Front: look from below the caliper. Rear: look from the right rear. Replace when either pad reaches the wear indicator; always replace both pads in a caliper.
Front: remove the pad pin, swap the pads so they sit on the caliper bracket and bracket pin, refit the pin (17 N·m) with silicone grease on the new boot.
Rear: same procedure; pad pin 17 N·m.
Pump the lever and pedal before riding, and check the fluid level.
checks: Front disc min 3.0 mm, rear 3.5 mm (1-10)
pitfalls: Getting grease on the pads or disc.

guides.why: A full brake check catches hose damage, leaks and seized parts before they fail on the trail.
guides.when: Every 4,000 mi.
steps: Check the hoses, banjo fittings and calipers for leaks, cracks and chafing.
Check the lever and pedal feel: firm, not spongy, and they return freely.
Check disc thickness and warpage if you have calipers and a dial gauge.
Turn the key on and confirm the ABS light comes on, then goes off above 10 km/h (6 mph).
checks: Disc limits: front 3.0 mm, rear 3.5 mm, warpage 0.30 mm (1-10)

guides.why: The rear switch is adjustable; it should light the brake light just before the rear brake bites.
guides.when: Every 4,000 mi.
steps: Key on. Squeeze the front lever and press the rear pedal separately; the brake light must come on for each.
Adjust the rear switch so the light comes on just before braking starts. The front switch isn't adjustable (screw 1.2 N·m).

guides.why: A beam aimed too high dazzles oncoming traffic; too low and you can't see. It shifts after a load change.
guides.when: Every 4,000 mi, and after changing the load on the bike.
steps: With the bike loaded as you ride it, turn the aiming bolt on the headlight to move the beam up or down.
The aim bolt is 2.0 N·m.

guides.why: The automatic centrifugal clutch has a manual adjuster on the right crankcase cover. If it is misadjusted, it slips or creeps.
guides.when: At 600 mi and every 4,000 mi, and after any right crankcase cover work.
steps: The adjuster is the screw and lock nut on the right crankcase cover.

From the Common Service Manual (2-36, centrifugal clutch): loosen the lock nut and back the adjuster bolt out about 1 turn (the book prints "tighten" here, but the next step only makes sense if you loosen it first), then turn it in until you just feel resistance. From there, back it out 1/8 turn, hold the bolt so it doesn't turn, and tighten the lock nut to 12 N·m. Test the clutch afterward.
Test: shifting should be smooth with no creep at idle in gear.
pitfalls: Riding with the adjuster too tight keeps the clutch partly disengaged and burns it.

guides.why: The sidestand switch cuts the engine if you put it in gear with the stand down.
guides.when: Every 4,000 mi.
steps: Check the stand swings freely and the spring isn't stretched or damaged. Grease the pivot.
With the engine running in gear, lowering the stand should stop the engine. If not, check the switch.
checks: Pivot bolt 18 N·m, pivot nut 44 N·m (1-13)

guides.why: Leaking fork seals and worn shock bushings are common after rough roads.
guides.when: Every 4,000 mi.
steps: Pump the fork hard with the front brake on: it should be smooth with no knock. Look for oil on the fork tubes.
Bounce the rear and check both shocks for leaks; check the mounting bolts.
Lift the rear and rock the swingarm side to side for play in the pivot.
Fork oil service (not on the schedule): 10W fork fluid, 120 cm³ per leg, level 140 mm.
checks: Shock nuts: upper 44 N·m, lower 29 N·m; swingarm pivot 54 N·m (1-14)

guides.why: On the stock muffler, the screen clogs with carbon and chokes the exhaust.
guides.when: Clean every 4,000 mi (USA models).

parts.name: Gasket A, ex. pipe
parts.note: #2 on the 2022 muffler diagram: the ring between the spark arrester and the muffler

steps: Let the muffler cool fully.
Remove the muffler cover, then the tail cap cover.
Remove the 3 spark arrester bolts, the arrester and the gasket.
Brush the carbon off the screen without tearing it. Replace the arrester if it has holes.
Refit with a new gasket: arrester bolts 9.0 N·m, tail cap 12 N·m, muffler cover 9.0 N·m.

guides.why: Vibration loosens fasteners on a single. A periodic sweep with a torque wrench catches them.
steps: Go over the chassis and engine mounts with the Torque tab of this page: axles, pinch bolts, handlebar, engine hangers (59 N·m), shocks, swingarm, caliper and brake hose bolts.
For anything not listed, use standard torque by thread size (6 mm flange 12 N·m, 8 mm 27 N·m, 10 mm 39 N·m).
Don't re-torque pre-coated (ALOC) bolts; replace them if they have been removed.
pitfalls: Re-torquing a bolt that was installed with threadlocker breaks the bond.

guides.why: Tires and spokes take the hardest beating on a trail bike. Loose spokes and low pressure lead to rim damage.
guides.when: Every 4,000 mi (**: Honda recommends a dealer for wheel work), and check pressures before every ride.
steps: Cold pressures: front 25 psi (175 kPa), rear 33 psi (225 kPa), rider only.
Replace a tire when the tread wear indicators show; check for cuts and bulges.
Tap each spoke: they should all ring the same. Spoke torque: front 3.2 N·m, rear 3.7 N·m.
Spin each wheel and check for wobble (rim runout limit 1.0 mm) and wheel bearing play.
Axle nuts: front and rear 59 N·m. After front wheel work, check the ABS sensor air gap (0.54-1.04 mm).
pitfalls: Non-stock tire sizes can set ABS code 7-1.

guides.why: Worn or loose head bearings make the steering notchy or let the front end clunk under braking.
guides.when: At 8,000, 16,000 and 24,000 mi. Honda recommends a dealer.
tools: Centerstand plus something to lift the front wheel
steps: Lift the front wheel off the ground. Turn the bars lock to lock: they should move smoothly with no notch at center.
Grip the fork bottoms and push and pull front to back: there must be no play.
If it needs adjusting: tighten the top thread to 27 N·m, turn lock to lock several times, loosen it completely, retighten by hand, then torque the stem nut to 88 N·m.
checks: Top thread 27 N·m then hand-tight; stem nut 88 N·m (3-25)
pitfalls: A notch at center means the bearings are already damaged; adjusting won't fix it.

pages.t: Technical features — fuel pump system with fuel filter blockage reminder
pages.s: The in-tank fuel pump draws through a fuel filter. If the filter clogs, fuel is drawn through a breather passage instead; once fuel level drops below the breather filter, air is drawn in and the engine runs lean/stumbles ('lack of fuel') as a reminder to replace the filter. There is no fixed filter-replacement interval. Driveability stays normal while fuel is above the breather filter. If fuel is sufficient but you get poor performance, fuel starvation or no-start, perform the fuel supply test.

pages.t: Fuel line — relieving pressure, disconnecting/connecting the quick-connect fitting; fuel supply test
pages.s: How to depressurize the fuel system and disconnect the resin fuel feed hose quick-connect fitting at the pump, and the order of tests if the engine is starved of fuel.

f.c: Fuel pump 5P connector location and quick-connect fitting retainer (push tab forward, press retainer down, pull off)
f.parts: fuel pump 5P connector, fuel tank cover area, fuel feed hose quick-connect fitting, retainer tab, plastic bags covering open ends

n: Fuel feed hose is resin — do not bend or twist it.
To depressurize: remove fuel tank cover (3-9), disconnect fuel pump 5P connector, start engine and let it idle until it stops, turn ignition OFF, disconnect battery negative (4-44).
Do not use tools to remove the connector; alternately pull and push until it comes off. Cover the fitting with a shop towel.
Check retainer condition; replace the fuel hose if needed. Cover disconnected ends with plastic bags.
Reconnect until the retainer clicks; a little engine oil on the pipe end helps. Pull to confirm it is locked.
After reassembly, turn ignition ON (don't start) — pump runs ~2 s; repeat 2-3 times and check for leaks.
Fuel supply test order: fuel pressure test (2-3) → if pressure OK, fuel flow inspection (2-3) → fuel flow inspection at specified fuel quantity (2-3).
